questions.question: In 12 Schedules — Complete Mastery Day, this exam clue belongs to which area: "1st Schedule: Names of all 28 States + 8 UTs. Article 1+4 refer to it. 2nd Schedule: Emoluments(salaries+allowances) of President, Vice-President, Governors, Supreme..."?
questions.explanation: Schedules 1–4: 1st Schedule: Names of all 28 States + 8 UTs. Article 1+4 refer to it. 2nd Schedule: Emoluments(salaries+allowances) of President, Vice-President, Governors, Supreme Court judges, HC judges, CAG, Speaker+Deputy Speaker of LS, Chairman+Deputy Chairman of RS. 3rd Schedule: Forms of Oaths and Affirmations for MPs, Ministers, Presidents, Judges. 4th Schedule: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States and UTs.

questions.question: In 12 Schedules — Complete Mastery Day, this exam clue belongs to which area: "5th Schedule: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas (for SCs/STs in states OTHER than NE states). Governor has special role — can make Regulations. 6th Schedule..."?
questions.explanation: Schedules 5–6: 5th Schedule: Administration and control of Scheduled Areas (for SCs/STs in states OTHER than NE states). Governor has special role — can make Regulations. 6th Schedule: Administration of Tribal Areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram ONLY. Has Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) with legislative+judicial powers. KEY DIFFERENCE : 5th: rest of India SCs/STs. 6th: ONLY 4 NE states tribal areas.

questions.question: In 12 Schedules — Complete Mastery Day, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Union List: 97 subjects (now effectively 100 after amendments). Centre has EXCLUSIVE power. Defence, Foreign affairs, Railways, Atomic energy, Banking, Insurance..."?
questions.explanation: 7th Schedule — MOST IMPORTANT: Union List: 97 subjects (now effectively 100 after amendments). Centre has EXCLUSIVE power. Defence, Foreign affairs, Railways, Atomic energy, Banking, Insurance, Currency. State List : 61 subjects (originally 66). States have power BUT Centre can legislate in national interest(Art 249), emergency(Art 250), state request(Art 252). Police, Public order, Land, Agriculture, Public health. Concurrent List : 52 subjects(originally 47). BOTH Centre+States can legislate. Centre prevails in case of conflict(Art 254). Education, Forests, Marriage, Electricity, Labour, Bankruptcy.

questions.question: In 12 Schedules — Complete Mastery Day, this exam clue belongs to which area: "8th Schedule: 22 Official Languages. Original: 14 languages(1950). Added : Sindhi(21st Amdt 1967), Konkani+Manipuri+Nepali(71st Amdt 1992)..."?
questions.explanation: Schedules 8–10: 8th Schedule: 22 Official Languages. Original: 14 languages(1950). Added : Sindhi(21st Amdt 1967), Konkani+Manipuri+Nepali(71st Amdt 1992), Bodo+Dogri+Maithili+Santhali(92nd Amdt 2003). English is NOT in 8th Schedule(it is associate official language for 15 yrs, extended indefinitely). 9th Schedule: 284 Acts protected from judicial review. Added by 1st Amdt(1951). BUT : SC in I.R. Coelho(2007) held laws added after Apr 24, 1973(Kesavananda date) can be reviewed if they violate Basic Structure. 10th Schedule: Anti-defection law. Added by 52nd Amdt(1985). Speaker/Chairman decides disqualification. Exception : merger of 2/3 of legislative party.

questions.question: In 12 Schedules — Complete Mastery Day, this exam clue belongs to which area: "11th Schedule: 29 subjects of Panchayati Raj Institutions. Added by 73rd Amdt(1992). Examples : Agriculture, Primary education, Rural housing, Drinking water..."?
questions.explanation: Schedules 11–12: 11th Schedule: 29 subjects of Panchayati Raj Institutions. Added by 73rd Amdt(1992). Examples : Agriculture, Primary education, Rural housing, Drinking water, Social forestry. 12th Schedule: 18 subjects of Urban Local Bodies(Municipalities). Added by 74th Amdt(1992). Examples : Urban planning, Roads+bridges, Public health, Slum improvement, Fire services. TRICK : 11th: 29 subjects(PR), 12th: 18 subjects(ULB). Higher number schedule : fewer subjects.

lesson_intro: Yesterday you saw all 12 Schedules for the first time. Today you drill them until they are instinctive. Here is why this matters: UPSC, in nearly every Prelims paper, has at least one question that asks "which Schedule deals with X?" or "which of the following is in the Concurrent List?" If you spend one full day on Schedules now, you will never lose a Schedule-based question for the rest of your preparation. The most important is the 7th Schedule — the division of legislative powers between Centre and States. It is the foundation for understanding Centre-State relations, which is covered in Day 15. Today, think of yourself as memorizing the index of India's most important document.
